paragraphs: In the club hour, the Explorers read an email from their pen pal, Nadia, in Singapore. "My grandma tells this story," she wrote. "It is about a swan and a butterfly." Mia loved animals, so she read the story out loud.

Long ago, a small butterfly lived next to a big lake. One day, a strong wind blew her far over the water. She was tired, and she could not see the land. The lake was wide, and no one was near. Her wings were very heavy. She began to fall toward the lake.

A white swan saw her and swam under her. The swan was kind, and her wings were strong. "Sit on my back," said the swan. "I will take you home." "I am so small, and you are so big," said the butterfly. "Why do you help me?" "Everyone needs help sometimes," said the swan. They flew up into the air. The view was beautiful, with green hills and a blue lake. The butterfly looked up at the stars in space and smiled. At last, she saw her flower garden and her family. She told her family about the kind swan.

The next winter, a thick fog came to the lake. The swan could not find her way home. The butterfly saw her from the garden. She called all her family and friends. They did not forget the swan's help. Hundreds of butterflies flew over the water together. Their colorful wings made a bright path in the fog. The swan followed the path and came home. "Thank you, my small friend," she said.

Teacher Kim smiled at the children. The children thought about the story for a minute. "What is the theme of this story?" she asked. "Be kind," said Mia. "Kind people get help too," said Lily. That evening, Lily wrote back to Nadia. "Please thank your grandma for the story," she wrote.
text.summary: Nadia, a pen pal, sends the Explorers a story from her grandma. A swan helps a tired butterfly, and later the butterflies help the swan, so the theme is to be kind.
